api:
<Spectrogram data={samples} x={|s: &Sample| s.time} value={|s: &Sample| s.value} window_size={512} />
PropTypeDefault
dataVec<T>, Signal<Vec<T>>, or your own Datasetrequired
xFn(&T) -> f64: time, in seconds, evenly spacedrequired
valueFn(&T) -> f64: the signalrequired
window_sizeusize: samples per FFT, rounded up to a power of two256
overlapf64: the share of each window that the next one repeats, 0 to 0.950.5
schemeHeatmapSchemeMagma
classTailwind classes ("h-64")

The signal is cut into windows, each window gets a Hann taper and a fast Fourier transform, and each cell is the power at that time and frequency in dB. The sample rate is taken from the median gap between x values; the y axis runs from 0 Hz to half the sample rate.

examples.title: Rising tone
examples.description: A chirp from 50 to 400 Hz over a constant 120 Hz hum, in dB.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn sweep() {
    let data = use_signal(chirp(2., 1000.));
    rsx! { <Spectrogram data={data} x={|s: &Sample| s.time} value={|s: &Sample| s.value} class="h-72" /> }
}
